## What it will cover

::: {.mm-stub-outline}
- Molecules as graphs: atoms as nodes, bonds as edges, featurisation
- Message passing and readout, step by step
- A minimal GNN in PyTorch (Geometric)
- Training on MoleculeNet tasks with proper splits
- GNN versus fingerprint baselines: a fair comparison
- Lab 7: train a GNN for solubility and inspect its learned embeddings
:::

## Planned learning outcomes

1. Featurise a molecule as a graph and explain message passing in your own words.
2. Train and evaluate a graph neural network on a molecular property task.
3. Decide, with evidence, whether a GNN is worth it over a fingerprint model for a given dataset size.

## In the meantime

Everything here builds on Part I, in particular the evaluation habits of [Chapter 2](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/index.html). Episode [2.6](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/06-pipelines-leakage.html) already introduces the group splits that become scaffold splits here.
